candidates.title: Compare action-level credit for context-management training
candidates.rule: When training agents to edit working context, compare fine-grained action credit with trajectory-level rewards after holding the context-editing tools and rollout strategy fixed.
candidates.passage: Fine-grained credit assignment further improves over context-aware partial rollout across all four benchmarks
candidates.finding: Adding fine-grained credit to the context-aware partial-rollout setup improves Qwen3-8B on all four evaluated QA benchmarks. Earlier entropy-only and context-aware additions have mixed task effects.
candidates.conditions: Cumulative RL ablation after SFT, GRPO and partial-rollout variants. The change concerns training credit for context actions, not a new inference prompt.
candidates.limitations: Cumulative comparisons do not identify every interaction. Hyperparameters were not extensively searched, and evidence is mainly QA and deep search, not GUI or coding. Training cost is part of the intervention.
candidates.validation_test: Compare action-level and trajectory-level credit with identical tools, data and rollout budget; evaluate QA, lost evidence, context size and total training/inference spend.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
